sampling_model.design: Known fixed \(r=2\) Conflict Graph Design using the formal direct-effect conflict graph \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\), generated from independent desired-exposure coordinates in Perron-priority rank order.
sampling_model.units: One triangular array of \(n\) fixed labeled units with fixed graph and fixed potential outcomes; there is no super-population sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The only randomness is \(U_{n,i}\), and Algorithm 1 maps it to the realized binary assignment \(Z_n\).
sampling_model.overlap: The endpoint exposure probability is known exactly as \(q_{n,i}=(4\lambda_n)^{-1}t_n^{|B_{n,i}|}\); for edgeless \(G_n\), \(\lambda_n=1\), \(B_{n,i}=\varnothing\), and \(q_{n,i}=1/4\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no statistical nuisance functions; \(\lambda_n\), \(q_{n,i}\), and \(\mathbf V_n\) are design-computable.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.6 proves asymptotic normality when the maximum conflict degree is \(o(n^{1/9})\).
Proposition 5.8 constructs a direct-effect sequence whose standardized CGD estimator does not converge in distribution.
Propositions 5.3 and 5.4 establish additive and ratio consistency, respectively, for the spectral variance-bound estimator.
Corollary 5.7 gives conservative Wald coverage under the paper's sufficient CLT regime.

Theorem 2.3 gives a Kolmogorov bound for dependency-graph sums with finite \(L^{\delta}\) moments for \(\delta\in[3,\infty)\); the direct fourth-moment substitution here sets \(\delta=4\). Theorem 2.1 is the bounded-summand result, and Theorem 2.4 treats \(\delta\in(2,3)\), so neither is the direct comparison for this class.
The discrete-time theorem bounds martingale normal approximation using increment moments and normalized predictable quadratic variation.
The paper characterizes admissible estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs.
The preprint derives design-based upper and lower bounds on minimax mean-squared point-estimation risk in terms of local and global conflict-graph connectivity.

body.tldr: For the fixed \(r=2\) Conflict Graph Design estimator, the candidate field-tier answer is a sharp uniform normal-inference frontier at \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\), with a quantitative prefix-sensitive martingale bound, a repeated-star Gaussian--Poisson obstruction at the boundary, uniform ratio consistency for the published spectral variance-bound estimator, and conservative feasible Wald coverage. Every new bound, boundary law, frontier, and expanded-regime inference claim remains a to-prove presolve target: D0 must independently validate the rank-indexed Doob identity, the coordinate-flip/operator chain, and the repeated-star limit before the exponent or absence of a slowly varying factor is accepted.

project_justification.gap: The published CGD theorem proves normality only under \(d_{\max}=o(n^{1/9})\), while its counterexample lies in a much denser regime; later generic dependency bounds do not resolve the intervening CGD-specific range.
project_justification.niche: Algorithm 1 is generated from ordered independent desired-exposure coordinates, which suggests a rank-indexed martingale structure hidden by reduction to two-hop dependency neighborhoods.
project_justification.fill: The project tests the candidate prefix-sensitive martingale bound against legal critical repeated-star failures and, only if both survive D0, carries the resulting iff frontier through the observable spectral variance bound to conservative Wald coverage.

body.related_work: \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} supplies the fixed \(r=2\) design, estimator, spectral variance bound, \(o(n^{1/9})\) sufficient CLT in Theorem 5.6, direct-effect nonconvergence construction in Proposition 5.8, additive consistency in Proposition 5.3, ratio consistency in Proposition 5.4, and Wald result in Corollary 5.7. Its formal direct-effect conflict graph has operator \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\); Appendix D.9 writes the star value as \(\sqrt{n-1}\) by suppressing the formal loop contribution, whereas the exact loop-inclusive value is \(1+\sqrt{n-1}\). The candidate statements would strictly strengthen the published distributional and coverage results if D0 verifies them. \cite{HeydeBrown1970DepartureNormality} and \cite{Haeusler1988MartingaleRate} supply the martingale normal-approximation template, while \cite{Bolthausen1982ExactMartingaleRates} and \cite{Mourrat2013MartingaleRate} clarify why conditional-variance fluctuations can govern exact behavior. Theorem 2.3 of \cite{JanischLehericy2024SparseDependencyGraph}, specialized to \(\delta=4\), is the direct finite-fourth-moment dependency-graph substitution; Theorem 2.1 applies only to bounded summands, and Theorem 2.4 addresses \(\delta\in(2,3)\). These results, together with \cite{Ross2011FundamentalsStein}, \cite{Chin2019SteinInterference}, and \cite{CaiShaoZhang2026RefinedLocalDependence}, inform the comparison but are not claimed to be sharpened as general probability theorems. \cite{KandirosHarshawSavje2026MinimaxNetwork} optimizes assignment designs and estimators for minimax mean-squared point-estimation risk under arbitrary neighborhood interference; it does not study the fixed \(r=2\) CGD estimator's Kolmogorov frontier or Wald coverage. \cite{AronowSamii2017GeneralInterference} provides the exposure-weighted design-based inference baseline. \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance} explains why inference targets an estimable conservative quadratic bound rather than the generally unidentified exact variance. Declaration 18.13 of \cite{BlairCoppockHumphreys2023ResearchDesign}, modeled after \cite{GreenKrasnoCoppockFarrerLenoirZingher2016LawnSigns}, supplies a concrete direct-effect consumer: its \(238\)-precinct queen-adjacency design defines \(\operatorname{mean}(Y_{1,0}-Y_{0,0})\), exactly the endpoint contrast considered here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The \(n^{2/3}\) exponent is not an established result. Presolve algebra and finite graph-family enumeration motivate, but do not prove, the rank-indexed identity or \(\mathrm{lem:prefix\text{-}flip\text{-}moments}\). D0 must independently derive the formula with \(\pi_n\) unit-to-rank, \(\rho_n=\pi_n^{-1}\), and \(\mathcal F_{n,s}=\sigma(U_{n,\rho_n(1)},\ldots,U_{n,\rho_n(s)})\), then prove or refute the shared-child orientation \(\mathsf P_n\operatorname{diag}(w_n)\mathsf P_n^{\top}\), the square-difference constants, the Bernoulli tensorization factor, and the imported martingale inequality. It must also verify the repeated-star Gaussian--Poisson law. Failure under arbitrary signed endpoints withdraws the candidate frontier and all expanded-regime ratio and coverage consequences without adding assumptions.
body.honest_scope: The fixed \(r=2\) design, estimator algebra, endpoint class, and published spectral variance-bound target are settled inputs. Every new formal statement is marked \(\text{to-prove}\). In particular, \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\), the absence of a slowly varying boundary factor, the repeated-star law, the prefix-flip envelope, uniform ratio consistency beyond the published regime, and expanded-regime Wald coverage are conjectural presolve targets pending independent D0 verification. The target is a worst-case maximum-degree iff frontier, not a necessary condition for each graph sequence. The interval remains conservative because \(\mathrm{VB}_n\) can exceed \(\sigma_n^2\), and no exact-coverage or exact-variance-estimation claim is made. The theorem would be an asymptotic benchmark for future CGD replications and would not retroactively validate the Bernoulli assignment or Aronow--Samii intervals in Declaration 18.13.
